newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes firmer in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes firmer in light trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar finished another somnolent day a touch higher against the U.S. dollar.
At the close, the Taiwan dollar was quoted at T$27.486, unchanged from the open and marginally higher that Thursday's T$27.49 close.
Turnover slipped to US$159 million from US$199 million.
Dealers complained that the central bank's seemingly tight grip on the exchange rate was squeezing life out of the Taiwan dollar market.
"We have been in doldrums since May," said a foreign bank dealer. "Nobody expects any change soon."

Military manoeuvres mounted by rival China to intimidate Taiwan in 1995 and early 1996 caused a period of turbulence for the Taiwan dollar in March and April, triggering heavy government intervention to protect the currency.
The central bank changed strategy in late April, however, making clear it wanted a weaker Taiwan dollar to spark Taiwan's crucial but flagging export sector.

According to the official statistics released on Wednesday, average daily spot volume in August was 17.7 percent lower than the same period last year. The currency eased for a month but has rebounded to the central bank's old T$27.5 defence level.
Also depriving the Taiwan dollar of direction was the U.S. dollar's stagnation ahead of September U.S. payroll data, which was not to be released until long after Taiwan's Friday close.
A Reuters survey of economists yielded average forecasts of 166,000 new U.S. jobs created in September against 250,000 in August, and joblessness rising to 5.2 percent from 5.1 percent.
